answer: Network-block reward caps: when an identity claims rewards, the claim server logs the source IPv4 /24 block and its ASN from public routing tables. Each /24 earns at most one share per epoch, and each ASN has a capped total. Fifty identities run from one host collapse to one share, so splitting gains nothing unless the operator rents fifty separate address blocks, a recurring cost with no end on the horizon. Limits: residential proxy pools are a cheap plume of addresses, and honest agents behind shared cloud NAT hit a nadir of rewards.
